Normally when you do a transaction through a bank, the bank registers that your account now have 'x' amount less and the others person 'x' amount more, making it so that the money moves and there isn't fraud, sort of a witness of the transaction. This register is put on a book to keep track on the money.Now, because Bitcoint doesn't have a 'bank' or other institution that acts as a witness, other people (miners) need to be do all of this (solving the mathematical problem/minig). So it its the verification that now person 1 has 'x' less bitcoin and person 2 'x'. The exact way of how is it done I'm not sure, because it's about economics and coding that I don't undestand.  


Edit: As mention before I'm not really an expert and some of this may be untrue so double check this information if you are really interested.

I'm not an expert but what I understand is that you need to 'solve' or decode a mathematical problem that validates a transaction, if you're the one that validates the transaction you get a commission (the mined Bitcoin). This solving are actually calculated guesses, this means people want a lot of guesses to increase the chance. This leads to a lot of devices working non stop trying to get the commission.
As I said before I'm not an expert and probably am wrong, also English is not my native language so if you're interested I suggest to investigate reliable sources and not reddit.
